paper.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning

result.summary: 本文挑战了复杂推理需要海量训练数据的假设，提出 Less-Is-More Reasoning (LIMO) 假说：在预训练已编码丰富领域知识的基础模型中，复杂推理可通过少量精心设计的认知过程示范被激发 [abstract][S1.p3]。作者通过多层筛选构建了仅 800 条样本的 LIMO 数据集，并对 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 进行简单监督微调 [S1.p4]。实验显示 LIMO 在 AIME24 上达到 63.3%、MATH500 上达到 95.6%，超过此前微调模型，且仅使用其 1% 的训练数据 [abstract][S1.p4]。LIMO 还在多种分布外基准上表现优异，平均性能达 78.1%，优于使用百倍以上数据训练的模型 [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：复杂推理是否真的需要海量训练数据，还是可以通过少量高质量样本激发。作者指出，传统范式基于两个假设——掌握复杂认知过程需要大量监督示范，以及监督微调主要导致记忆而非真正泛化 [S1.p1]。作者认为这种数据密集型范式可能不再必要，因为现代基础模型已在预训练中编码大量数学知识，挑战从知识获取转变为知识激发 [S1.p2]。

evidence.quote: Complex reasoning has long been considered one of the most challenging capabilities to instill in large language models (LLMs).

first, that mastering such complex cognitive processes requires extensive supervised demonstrations, and second, that supervised fine-tuning leads primarily to memorization rather than true generalization.
We argue this data-intensive paradigm may no longer be necessary.
Contemporary LLMs may already possess rich mathematical knowledge, transforming the challenge from knowledge acquisition to knowledge elicitation.

method.text: 论文提出 LIMO 假说，认为在预训练已全面编码领域知识的基础模型中，复杂推理可通过少量但精确编排的认知过程示范涌现，其激发阈值取决于模型预训练知识库的完整性和后训练样本作为“认知模板”的有效性 [abstract][S3.p1]。方法上，作者构建了一个多层筛选的数据 curation 流程：先进行粗粒度难度过滤，再进行细粒度难度评估，并进行知识点多样化，同时根据逻辑连贯性、步骤清晰度和解答准确性筛选推理链，最终得到 800 条训练样本 [S1.p4]。随后使用简单监督微调在 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 上训练 [S1.p4][S4.p2]。

evidence.quote: In foundation models where domain knowledge has been comprehensively encoded during pre-training, sophisticated reasoning can emerge through minimal but strategically designed demonstrations of cognitive processes.

In foundation models where domain knowledge has been comprehensively encoded during pre-training, sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through minimal but precisely orchestrated demonstrations of cognitive processes.

first conducting coarse difficulty filtering to eliminate trivial problems, then fine-grained difficulty assessment to identify challenging questions, followed by knowledge point diversification to ensure comprehensive coverage.
This meticulous process yields a compact yet potent dataset of just 800 training samples.
With simple supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using only this curated dataset based on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct
We fine-tune Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct using supervised fine-tuning on our LIMO dataset.

experiments.text: 论文在域内和分布外基准上评估模型。域内评估包括 AIME24、MATH500 和 AMC23 [S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1]。分布外评估包括 OlympiadBench、中文多语言基准 CHMath、Gaokao、Kaoyan、GradeSchool，以及多学科基准 Minerva 和 GPQA [S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1]。评估使用 pass@1 指标，在零样本思维链设置下进行；较大基准使用贪心解码单样本，较小基准生成 4 个样本并计算无偏 pass@1 [S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1]。基线包括 OpenAI-o1-preview、QwQ-32B-Preview、Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct，以及使用 OpenThoughts-114k 和 NuminaMath-100k 微调的模型 [S6.SS1.p1][S6.SS1.p2]。

evidence.quote: Our primary evaluation suite includes several well-established mathematical competitions and benchmarks: the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME24), MATH500, and the American Mathematics Competitions (AMC23).
First, we include diverse mathematical competitions like OlympiadBench to test performance on different mathematical challenges.

we construct novel multilingual benchmarks using recent examination problems: CHMath (2024 Chinese High School Mathematics League), Gaokao (China’s 2024 College Entrance Exam), Kaoyan (Chinese Graduate School Entrance Exams), and GradeSchool (our new elementary mathematics benchmark).
Third, we incorporate multi-disciplinary benchmarks including Minerva (undergraduate-level STEM) and GPQA
We evaluate performance using the pass@1 metric in a zero-shot chain-of-thought setting across all benchmarks.
For larger benchmarks (MATH500, OlympiadBench, Gaokao, Kaoyan, GradeSchool, MinervaMath, and GPQA), we employ greedy decoding with a single sample.
For smaller benchmarks (less than 50 problems: AIME24, AMC23, and CHMath), we generate 4 samples (temperature=0.6) and calculate the unbiased pass@1 metric.

These include OpenAI-o1-preview, a large language model that has demonstrated advanced mathematical reasoning abilities across various complex tasks; QwQ-32B-Preview, a model specifically designed for mathematical problem-solving with strong reasoning capabilities; and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, which serves as our base model for comparative analysis.

These comparative datasets include OpenThoughts-114k, a synthetic reasoning dataset containing 114k examples covering mathematics, science, coding, and puzzles, with solutions following a structured reasoning format generated by DeepSeek-R1; and NuminaMath-100k, a randomly selected 100k subset of NuminaMath-CoT

findings.text: LIMO 在域内任务上取得最佳结果：AIME24 准确率 63.3%，MATH500 准确率 95.6%，AMC23 准确率 96.3%，均超过 QwQ-32B-Preview 和 OpenAI-o1-preview [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1]。在分布外任务上，LIMO 在 OlympiadBench 达到 67.6%，CHMath 达到 84.2%，GradeSchool 达到 76.2%，GPQA 达到 70.7% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1]。与更大数据集相比，NuminaMath-100k 出现显著退化（32.3%），OpenThoughts-114k 结果次优（58.3%），而 LIMO 的 800 条精选问题取得更优性能（78.1%）[S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1]。LIMO 在所有基准上平均性能最高，达 78.1% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1]。

evidence.quote: On in-domain tasks, LIMO achieves the best results across all benchmarks.
For AIME24, LIMO achieves 63.3% accuracy, outperforming QwQ-32B-Preview (50.0%) and OpenAI-o1-preview (44.6%) by significant margins.
On MATH500, LIMO achieves a notable 95.6% accuracy, surpassing QwQ-32B-Preview (89.8%) and OpenAI-o1-preview (85.5%).
The performance gap is even more pronounced on AMC23, where LIMO reaches 96.3% accuracy compared to QwQ-32B-Preview’s 83.6%.
On OlympiadBench, LIMO achieves 67.6% accuracy, significantly outperforming QwQ-32B-Preview (58.5%) and the base model (45.3%).
Similar improvements are observed on other challenging benchmarks such as CHMath (84.2% vs 68.5%) and GradeSchool (76.2% vs 63.8%).
Notably, LIMO maintains competitive performance even on GPQA, where it achieves 70.7% accuracy, close to OpenAI-o1-preview’s leading score of 73.3%.

NuminaMath-100k shows significant degradation (32.3% vs. base model’s 49.9%) due to uncurated reasoning chains, while OpenThoughts-114k achieves suboptimal results (58.3%) probably due to unfocused problem selection.

In contrast, LIMO’s carefully curated 800 problems yield superior performance (78.1%), demonstrating that targeted selection are more crucial than data quantity for developing robust reasoning capabilities.
LIMO achieves the highest average performance of 78.1% across all benchmarks, substantially outperforming OpenAI-o1-preview, QwQ-32B-Preview, and other baselines.

limitations.text: 作者在样本效率分析中指出，维持有效性能的最低数据量下界仍是一个开放问题 [S6.SS3.SSS5.p1]。此外，作者提到未来工作可以探索主动学习策略以进一步优化样本效率 [S6.SS3.SSS5.p2]。

evidence.quote: though the lower bound for maintaining effective performance remains an open question.
Future work could explore active learning strategies to further optimize sample efficiency.
